title: Software and distributed systems
task_statement: Design model calls as remote calls with timeouts, retries, error handling, and streams. (Inference: task wording from repo lesson 7-1A, not from the exam guide)

components.name: Error classes and retry
components.first_principle: Each error type tells the caller whether a retry can help.
steps: The API returns an HTTP status code and an error type for each failure.
A 400 invalid_request_error means the request needs a fix, so a retry does not help.
A 401 authentication_error means the key needs a fix, so a retry does not help.
A 429 rate_limit_error can succeed after a wait.
A 500 api_error or a 529 overloaded_error is a transient 5xx failure, so a retry with backoff can help.
Read the retry-after header and wait that many seconds before the next attempt.
Record the request-id from each failed response.
pros: Typed errors separate faults that need a fix from faults that clear with time.
The official SDK retries transient failures with backoff by default.
The request ID links an error to the server-side record.
cons: A spend-cap 429 does not clear with a retry.
Retries add load when the service is already under stress.
An error can arrive inside a 200 stream after the status line.
use_when: A call fails with 429, 500, or 529 and the request is valid.
A service calls the API and needs a bounded retry policy.
do_not_use_when: The error is a 400 invalid_request_error. Fix the request first.
The 429 has no retry-after header and comes from a spend cap.

constraints.choice: Log the request ID and error type for each failure.
constraints.combination: Alert when 529 errors rise above a set rate. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Honor the retry-after header on 429 responses.
constraints.combination: Request a tier increase when 429 retries stay high.

constraints.choice: Set a fixed number of retries for each request.
constraints.combination: Stop retries when the user time budget ends. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Increase traffic in steps to avoid acceleration limits.

components.trap: A prompt that says try again looks like a retry policy, but the model cannot resend the request or read a retry-after header.
components.decision_rule: Retry 429 and 5xx errors with a limit and backoff. Fix 400 and 401 errors first.
components.exam_tip: A 429 with retry-after means wait. A 429 with no retry-after header points to a spend cap.

components.name: Timeouts and long requests
components.first_principle: A request that runs too long can lose its connection, so long work uses a stream or a batch.
steps: Use streaming for a long response, so your app reads events as they arrive.
The SDK checks that a Messages request that does not stream is not expected to pass a 10-minute timeout.
Set a TCP keep-alive on direct integrations to reduce idle drops.
Create a Message Batch for work that the user does not wait for.
Poll the batch until processing_status is ended.
Download the results within 29 days of creation.
pros: Streaming lets your app process events as they arrive.
Batches let the caller poll for results instead of one open connection.
The SDK can return the complete message from a stream.
cons: A stream can fail mid-response, so the app must handle partial output.
Batches expire if processing does not finish within 24 hours.
Batch wait times vary, and most batches finish within 1 hour.
use_when: The response can run for many minutes and the user reads it as it arrives.
A job has many requests that can wait up to a day.
do_not_use_when: The user waits for a short answer. A standard request works.
The result must arrive in seconds. A batch is the wrong choice.

constraints.choice: Stream long responses that users read.
constraints.combination: Use batches when the user does not wait.

constraints.choice: Use batches for work that can wait, because batch requests cost 50 percent less.
Keep Messages API requests under 32 MB.
constraints.combination: Use the Batch API for payloads up to 256 MB.

constraints.choice: Track processing_status and the expiry time of each batch.
constraints.combination: Store the results before the 29-day window ends.

native_services.text: Bedrock streams over standard server-sent events on its Messages API endpoint.

Entra ID tokens typically expire after 1 hour, so long jobs need a token refresh.

components.decision_rule: Stream when the user waits, and batch when the caller can poll later.

components.name: Streaming events and errors
components.first_principle: A stream sends typed events after a 200 status, so an error can arrive inside the stream.
steps: The API sends server-sent events after a 200 status.
Ping events can appear at any point in the stream.
Delta events add partial content to a content block.
An error event can arrive in the stream, for example an overloaded_error.
Handle error events in the same loop that handles content events.
The SDK can assemble the complete message from the stream.
For Claude 4.5 models and earlier, an interrupted stream can resume from the point where it stopped.
pros: Partial output reaches the user early.
The SDK returns a complete message when the app needs no events.
An overloaded_error in a stream uses the same type name as HTTP 529.
cons: Error handling must cover failures that arrive after the status line.
Partial text can show before the stream ends.
Resume is documented only for Claude 4.5 models and earlier.
use_when: The user reads output while the model writes it.
The app acts on partial tool input before the response ends.
do_not_use_when: A background job needs only the final message.
The client cannot parse server-sent events.

constraints.choice: Stream long responses to show the first tokens early.
constraints.combination: Use the SDK helper when the app needs no events.

constraints.choice: Log each error event type and the request ID.
constraints.combination: Send a new request on newer models, because resume is documented only for Claude 4.5 and earlier. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Treat streamed text as unverified until the final message arrives. (Inference)
Handle each event type in code.

native_services.text: The Messages API endpoint uses standard server-sent events, unlike the InvokeModel integration.

components.exam_tie: F3. Expect an option that treats a stream as one full response. The credited answer handles error events and partial text. (Inference)
components.trap: Only the HTTP status code looks sufficient, but a stream can fail after the 200 status.
components.decision_rule: Handle error events inside the stream loop. Do not rely on the HTTP status check alone.
components.exam_tip: An overloaded_error event inside a stream corresponds to HTTP 529 in a call that does not stream.

cheatsheet:
flowchart LR
  S[Status code] --> T{Transient?}
  T -->|Yes| B[Backoff with limit]
  T -->|No| F[Fix request]
  L[Long job] --> M{User waits?}
  M -->|Yes| ST[Stream]
  M -->|No| BA[Batch and poll]
  ST --> E[Handle error events]

patterns.wording: a call fails with a server error and the request is valid
patterns.answer_type: bounded retry with backoff in caller code
patterns.rule: Retry transient errors with a limit. Fix invalid requests first.

patterns.wording: a long job that no user waits for
patterns.rule: Create a batch and poll processing_status until it is ended.
traps: Thousands of synchronous calls in a loop

patterns.wording: partial output appears, then the call fails
patterns.rule: Handle error events inside the stream loop.
